claims.text: Stage-2's backup-db.sh runs pg_dump with --schema-only, which dumps only object definitions and no data, and the run exits 0.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2 scripts/terminal/backup-db.sh:11-12, outputs/stage-2/scripts/terminal/backup-db.txt; PostgreSQL 17 docs: pg_dump option -s/--schema-only

claims.text: When archive_command fails, PostgreSQL retries it periodically and unarchived WAL stays in pg_wal on the server's own disk, so clients see nothing different until that file system fills up (then PANIC shutdown).
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 25.3.1 Setting Up WAL Archiving (archive command failure, retries, pg_wal continues to fill)

claims.text: A backup job's success reports only on what it was asked to do, so a schema-only dump, a database missing from the list or a stalled WAL archive go unnoticed until a restore is attempted; testing a restore finds them. The WAL archive is tested by recovering from it.
claims.source_hint: Outline items 1-2; follows from claims 1-2 and backup-logical.sh:18 (fixed database list); devops.l3.point-in-time-recovery (recovery from the WAL archive)

claims.text: restore-test.sh lines 20-23 (stage-3) start postgres:17.6-alpine with docker run --detach --rm --network none, POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD=trust, the backups volume mounted read-only (:ro), and a trap on EXIT that removes the container.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 scripts/devops/restore-test.sh:20-23

claims.text: docker run --network none leaves the container only a loopback interface (127.0.0.1) and no external network, so it cannot reach other containers such as db; --rm removes the container when it exits.
claims.source_hint: Docker docs: Networking, 'none' network driver; docker run reference --rm

claims.text: psql, PostgreSQL's command-line client, runs globals.sql (roles) before the dumps, because the empty server has no donhang role and the dumped objects are owned by donhang; owning roles must exist before a restore.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 scripts/devops/restore-test.sh:29-30; PostgreSQL 17 docs: psql reference (Description); 25.1.1 Restoring the Dump (users owning dumped objects must already exist)

claims.text: pg_restore --create creates the database recorded in the archive and restores into it; the database named by --dbname is used only for the initial connection. initdb creates a postgres database in every new cluster.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: pg_restore option -C/--create; 22.2 Creating a Database / initdb (template0, template1, postgres)

claims.text: pg_restore --exit-on-error (-e) stops at the first error while sending SQL commands; by default pg_restore continues after errors and reports a count of errors at the end.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: pg_restore option -e/--exit-on-error

claims.text: Under set -e (set -euo pipefail at line 4), a failing pg_restore call in the for loop at lines 31-34 ends restore-test.sh with a non-zero exit status (the failing command's own status, not necessarily 1).
claims.source_hint: GNU Bash manual: The Set Builtin (-e); examples/don-hang @ stage-3 scripts/devops/restore-test.sh:4, 31-34

claims.text: restore-test.sh lines 39-53 read counts.txt, count each listed table in the restored donhang with SELECT count(*), print same or DIFFERENT, set failed=1 on any difference, print the elapsed seconds and exit with failed.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 scripts/devops/restore-test.sh:39-53

claims.text: counts.txt holds the rows of orders, order_items and customers counted inside donhang.dump itself by backup-logical.sh lines 28-37 (pg_restore --data-only --table piped to awk).
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 scripts/devops/backup-logical.sh:28-37

claims.text: The captured output shows five 'restored' lines (donhang, donhang_notifications, donhang_payments, donhang_tofu, keycloak), three 'same' lines with customers 5, and the elapsed time; '...' replaces unstable values.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/restore-test.txt; outputs/unstable.regex

claims.text: newest (line 8) is the newest dump directory; started (line 14) is set just after it is found. The printed time runs from started to the end of the check (line 52), so it includes starting the container.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 scripts/devops/restore-test.sh:8, 14, 20-27, 52

claims.text: Because expected counts come from the dump, the check proves the file restores what it holds, not that it holds everything; a database missing from backup-logical.sh's list, or a dump with no rows (0 = 0), would still pass.
claims.source_hint: Reasoning from examples/don-hang @ stage-3 scripts/devops/backup-logical.sh:18, 31-37 and restore-test.sh:31, 39-50

claims.text: The measured restore time is one part of the RTO (which also covers noticing the failure, getting a machine, pointing the api at it); if it alone exceeds the target, the target or the backup method must change.
claims.source_hint: Course definition of RTO (devops.l3.rpo-and-rto); outline item 4

claims.text: When backups run on a schedule, the restore test should run on a schedule too, with an alert when it fails, since a past pass says nothing about the newest backup; Đơn Hàng's lab runs it by hand only.
claims.source_hint: Outline item 5; depth_notes (no real scheduled job or alert in the lab)

claims.text: Restoring into a fresh server is more realistic than restoring over the live db: a disaster leaves an empty server; on db the donhang role already exists, hiding a missing globals.sql; restoring over live data replaces orders being written.
claims.source_hint: Outline misconception 2; claim 6; restore-test.sh:16-19 comment

claims.text: Exit status 0 from pg_dump means it completed without error; it does not check the chosen options against intent or that the file will restore on another server.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: pg_dump (Diagnostics / exit status); claims 1, 6

claims.text: POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD=trust makes the postgres image accept host connections without a password; with --network none no other machine can connect.
claims.source_hint: postgres Docker image docs: Environment Variables, POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD; PostgreSQL 17 docs: 20.4 Trust Authentication

claims.text: On first start the postgres image runs a temporary init server that listens on no TCP address (Unix socket only), then the real server; pg_isready checks whether a server accepts connections; restore-test.sh:25-27 loops until it does.
claims.source_hint: postgres Docker image docs / docker-entrypoint.sh (docker_temp_server_start, listen_addresses=''); PostgreSQL 17 docs: pg_isready; examples/don-hang @ stage-3 scripts/devops/restore-test.sh:25-27
